summary: CLI daemon exposes local PTY/shell to vendor-controlled WebSocket gateway
details: The package ships a CLI (bin 'whalent') whose runtime is delivered as heavily obfuscated bundles (dist/index.cjs and a ~4.8 MB dist/core.cjs produced with javascript-obfuscator: control-flow flattening, rotating string arrays, hex identifiers). On startup the daemon opens a persistent WebSocket to wss://memory.whalent.com/gw/sdk/ws and, per the package README, 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway'. The bundle imports @xterm/headless, node-pty, and ssh2, and contains ptyProcess/spawn code paths together with ssh.tunnel.open / proxy.open / preview.open handlers, giving whoever controls the gateway a path to drive a pseudo-terminal, spawn child processes, and open SSH tunnels/proxies on the host running the daemon. The obfuscation of the entire runtime prevents review of exactly which remote-dispatched operations the gateway can invoke. The channel is reachable only when a user explicitly runs the 'whalent' daemon with a token, not on 'npm install' or on library require, so the exposure is confined to hosts on which an operator starts the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
